newsitem.title: FRANCE: EC COMMISSIONER OPPOSES FRENCH DELAY ON EMU.
newsitem.headline: EC COMMISSIONER OPPOSES FRENCH DELAY ON EMU.

text.p: The European Union commissioner for monetary affairs insisted on Tuesday that an agreement on the single currency was needed at an EU summit next week despite a request for time by France's new left-wing government.
Commissioner Yves Thibault de Silguy, a Frenchman, said the EU needed to stick by the agreed schedule if the single European currency was to be credible.

"There must be an agreement now...The road to the single currency needs a clear view," he told France Inter radio a day after France asked for time to study a previously agreed pact to keep budget deficits tight after the currency is launched.
"Sticking to the schedule is important, otherwise we will signal a backtracking that would be very harmful for everyone, particularly for France," he said.

But France's European Affairs Minister Pierre Moscovici insisted Paris needed more than a week to study the EU stability pact, an integral part of its plans for economic and monetary union (EMU), and carry out an audit of state finances.
"If we request an assessment, it means it will take a bit more than one week," he told RMC radio.
The pact, agreed after hard-fought overnight negotiations in Dublin in December, was supposed to be ratified by EU leaders when they meet in Amsterdam next week.

Moscovici said it was only normal that Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, who took office last week after the left's parliamentary election victory and is to outline his policy on June 19, be given time to study texts that were approved before he came to office.

"We will see from an audit of state finances what is our room for manoeuvre," Moscovici said. "My conviction is that the state finances are not healthy. The audit will reveal this and from there we will have to work out a realistic budget."
He said the budget would include Jospin's campaign pledge to create 700,000 jobs for young people in order to curb record 12.8 percent unemployment.
Moscovici said the EU would need to take into account the change in the bloc's political balance after the coming to power of the Labvour party in Britain and the left in France.
"Social democrats have a majority, it is up to them to discuss and define a joint conception and convince the others," he said.

"We do not intend to start a crisis. We are here so that Europe moves forward, but also so that our European friends take our natIonal priorities into account. Moving towards Europe without undoing France was our campaign slogan and this slogan will be the government's line," he said.
